newsitem.title: USA: Residents return home after California derailment.
newsitem.headline: Residents return home after California derailment.

text.p: Residents were allowed to return home late Saturday after emergency crews hauled away many of the freight cars carrying gas residue and corrosive acid that jumped the tracks near Martinez, Calif. Friday, authorities said.
"It's a brute force operation to get them out," Contra Costa County Sheriff Lt. Scott Daly said of the effort to move the rail cars.

The derailment occurred late Friday about 25 miles (40 km) northeast of San Francisco. The two-locomotive, 60-car Burlington Northern Santa Fe train was traveling to nearby Richmond, Calif., when it jumped the tracks.
At least 19 cars of the train carrying gas residue and corrosive acid derailed in the accident. Several cars tumbled down a canyon slope near some homes.
The derailment forced the evacuation of residents within a half mile of the site. They were allowed to return to their homes late Saturday.
There have been no reports of injuries or leaks, and the cause of the derailment is still under investigation.

Burlington Northern crews worked through the night and all day Saturday to remove rail cars from the canyon area. The cleanup effort could take several days, Burlington Northern spokesman Michael Martin said.
"There still are cars in the area but they're away from the homes," Martin said.
Of the 19 freight cars that derailed, 10 contained liquefied petroleum gas residue, two were carrying phosphoric acid and one was full of paint.
Martin said the accident damaged a large section of track, forcing Burlington Northern to detour some of its trains.
But he said repairs were completed late Saturday, allowing crews to reopen the line, which carries 20 or more freight trains each day to and from the San Francisco Bay area.
